hook.speaker: Arjuna
hook.setting: Arjuna, seeing his own family in the enemy ranks, collapses in grief before the battle.
hook.sanskrit: सीदन्ति मम गात्राणि मुखं च परिशुष्यति । वेपथुश्च शरीरे मे रोमहर्षश्च जायते ॥ गाण्डीवं स्रंसते हस्तात्त्वक्चैव परिदह्यते । न च शक्नोम्यवस्थातुं भ्रमतीव च मे मनः ॥
hook.line: Shaking limbs, a dry mouth, a racing body: the Gita opens with a panic attack, not a hero.
hook.translation: My limbs give way, my mouth is parched, my body trembles and my hair stands on end.
hook.why: Even the strongest people freeze; the Gita begins with a breakdown, not a hero.
hook.misuse: Not a dismissal of anxiety; it shows that even the strong feel it, and the teaching starts there.

prasang.title: Overcome by delusion, Arjuna speaks in fear, love and grief
prasang.summary: Seeing his kin ready to die, Arjuna trembles, his bow slips, and he argues that no victory is worth killing family. He sits down in the chariot and refuses to fight.
prasang.story_hook: The greatest archer of his age stood between two armies, and his hands began to shake.
prasang.lesson: Even the strongest people freeze; the Gita begins with a breakdown, not a hero.

alternates.speaker: Arjuna
alternates.setting: Arjuna confesses the mind is as hard to hold as the wind; Krishna answers.
alternates.sanskrit: चञ्चलं हि मनः कृष्ण प्रमाथि बलवद्दृढम् । तस्याहं निग्रहं मन्ये वायोरिव सुदुष्करम् ॥
alternates.line: The mind is restless, stormy, stubborn and strong. Holding it feels like holding the wind.
alternates.translation: For the mind is restless, Krishna, turbulent, powerful and stubborn. I think it is as hard to hold as the wind.
alternates.why: The mind is hard to hold, but practice and letting go train it.

prasang.title: Mastering the mind
prasang.summary: Arjuna says the mind is restless, stormy and stubborn. Krishna agrees, and says practice and letting go can train it.
prasang.lesson: The mind is hard to hold, but practice and letting go train it.

alternates.speaker: Arjuna
alternates.setting: Arjuna, shown Krishna's cosmic form, is overwhelmed by its scale.
alternates.sanskrit: नभःस्पृशं दीप्तमनेकवर्णंव्यात्ताननं दीप्तविशालनेत्रम् । दृष्ट्वा हि त्वां प्रव्यथितान्तरात्माधृतिं न विन्दामि शमं च विष्णो ॥
alternates.line: Seeing something too big to take in, my heart trembles and I can't find steadiness or calm.
alternates.translation: Seeing you touching the sky, blazing with many colours, mouths wide open, with huge fiery eyes, my inner self trembles, Vishnu, and I find neither courage nor peace.
alternates.why: Facing something vast can shake you to the core, and that's human.

prasang.title: Arjuna sees the cosmic form and praises it
prasang.summary: Arjuna sees all beings, gods and worlds in Krishna, and warriors rushing into his mouths like moths into flame. Terrified, he asks who Krishna really is.
prasang.story_hook: Arjuna saw everything at once, and for the first time in his life he could not find his footing.
prasang.lesson: Facing something vast can shake you to the core, and that's human.

verse.speaker: Vishnu
verse.setting: Vishnu explains to the frightened gods where fear comes from.
verse.sanskrit: दीनताजं भयं माने गुणे खलभयं खलु । भयं निन्दकजं शक्तौ विद्यायां वादिनं भयम् ॥
verse.line: Honour fears disgrace, virtue fears the wicked, power fears critics, learning fears debate. Every gain brings a fear.
verse.translation: In honour lies the fear of being brought low; in virtue, the fear of the wicked; in power, the fear of critics; in learning, the fear of rival debaters.
verse.why: Every gain brings its own fear; holding things lightly is the way out.

prasang.title: Vishnu on where fear comes from
prasang.summary: The frightened gods ask Vishnu how to become fearless. He explains that every possession carries its own fear (the body fears age, wealth fears thieves, power fears critics) and that only dispassion is free of fear; then he restates Bhagavad Gita 2.14-15 on enduring pleasure and pain.
prasang.lesson: Every gain brings its own fear; holding things lightly is the way out.

verse.speaker: Tulsidas
verse.setting: Frightened by hard times, Tulsidas asks Ram to say the words he needs to hear.
verse.sanskrit: रीति सुनि रावरी प्रतीति-प्रीति रावरे सों, डरत हौं देखि कलिकालको कहरु। कहेही बनैगी कै कहाये, बलि जाउँ, राम, “तुलसी ! तू मेरो, हारि हिये न हहरु'॥
verse.line: "You are mine. Do not lose heart, do not tremble."
verse.translation: Having heard your ways, my trust and love are in you, yet I am afraid, seeing the cruelty of these times. It will only be well if you say it, or have it said, Ram: "Tulsi, you are mine. Do not lose heart, do not tremble."

verse.speaker: A brahmin (retold by Bhishma)
verse.setting: The brahmin tells the grieving King Senajit how to meet whatever life brings.
verse.sanskrit: सुखं वा यदि वा दुःखं प्रियं वा यदि वाऽप्रियम् / प्राप्तं प्राप्तमुपासीत हृदयेनापराजितः
verse.line: Pleasant or painful, meet whatever comes with a heart that refuses to be defeated.
verse.translation: Whether it is happiness or sorrow, something pleasant or unpleasant, meet whatever comes with a heart that is not defeated.
verse.why: No one suffers forever. Meet what comes with an undefeated heart.

verse.speaker: Vasishtha
verse.setting: The sage Vasishtha to Bharat, shattered by his father's death and Ram's exile.
verse.sanskrit: तात हृदयँ धीरजु धरहु करहु जो अवसर आजु। उठे भरत गुर बचन सुनि करन कहेउ सबु साजु ॥
verse.line: Keep courage in your heart, and do what today asks of you.
verse.translation: "Child, keep courage in your heart, and do what this moment asks of you today." Hearing his teacher, Bharat rose and had everything made ready.
verse.why: When head and heart disagree, go and face the person you think you wronged.

prasang.title: Bharat refuses the throne
prasang.summary: After the funeral, Vasishtha, the ministers and Kausalya all urge Bharat to rule, as his father wished. Bharat says the advice is right and his heart still isn't at peace; the crown means nothing without Ram. He decides to go to the forest, admit his fault, and trust his brother to forgive.
prasang.story_hook: Everyone agreed the throne was his, and Bharat could not bring himself to sit on it.
prasang.lesson: When head and heart disagree, go and face the person you think you wronged.

verse.speaker: Ribhu
verse.setting: Ribhu on inner stillness in an active life.
verse.sanskrit: बहिःकृत्रिमसंरंभो हृदि संरम्भवर्जितः । कर्ता बहिरकर्तान्तर्लोके विहर शुद्धधीः ॥
verse.line: Be busy on the outside and unhurried inside. Act fully, but don't let it agitate you.
verse.translation: Outwardly busy, inwardly free of agitation; a doer on the outside, a non-doer within: move through the world with a clear mind.
verse.why: Live fully in the world while staying unhurried inside.

prasang.title: How a free person lives
prasang.summary: Ribhu describes how a free person lives among others: letting go of what is lost, taking up what comes, doing the work at hand, speaking gently, busy outside and calm inside, and treating the whole world as family.
prasang.lesson: Live fully in the world while staying unhurried inside.

story.title: Six seekers wait a year
story.story_hook: Six seekers arrived with fuel in their hands and questions on their lips, and were told to wait a year.
story.summary: Six earnest seekers come to the sage Pippalada with questions. Instead of answering, he asks them to live with him for a year in discipline and faith, and only promises to answer what he actually knows.
story.lesson: Readiness matters, and a good teacher only claims what he knows.

anchor.line: The pure world belongs to those with no crookedness, no lying and no trickery in them.
anchor.translation: That stainless world of Brahman belongs to those in whom there is no crookedness, no falsehood and no deceit.
anchor.why: Readiness matters, and a good teacher only claims what he knows.
